commit_subject: ground policy surfaces in ingested sources
description: carer's allowance and carer support payment with the 35-hour and £204 earnings conditions

release_errors_before_success.error: No active corpus source found for 'uk/guidance/mygovscot/carer-support-payment/who-can-apply'

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module paid carer support payment on a PolicyEngine-shaped gate (in Scotland AND a rollout switch AND (35 care hours OR a reported carer's allowance amount)) and never applied the mygov.scot conditions that the carer be aged 16 or over, not in full-time education, caring for someone who gets a qualifying disability benefit, and have take-home pay of no more than £204 a week.
triage.triage_notes: Read the vendored source slices added in this commit (data/corpus/provisions/uk/guidance/2026-06-10-uk-mygovscot-carer-support-payment-{who-can-apply,if-you-work}.jsonl): they state "You can apply for Carer Support Payment if you provide unpaid care for 35 hours or more a week and you must be aged 16 or over", "The person you care for must get a qualifying disability benefit" and "Your 'take home pay' cannot be more than £204 a week", so the added conditions are source-required clauses that were missing. Two defects co-occur in the same module: besides the missing clauses, the pre-fix formula's `or reported_carers_allowance_for_year > 0` disjunct and the `carer_support_payment_in_effect` switch are untraceable branches (PolicyEngine reported receipt / rollout switch, no basis in the cited regulations) that the fix removes; a reviewer who prefers that framing should re-kind this as untraceable_branch. Module was also restructured into weekly + annual rules and the citation set moved from SSI 2023/302 regs 5/16 to mygov.scot guidance (the SSI rate/hours imports are kept). Boundary check: source says pay "cannot be more than £204", encoding uses <= 204 - consistent. Same commit-wide pattern as indices 1-6.
triage.verifier_justification: The diff changes encoded meaning exactly as the first reader described: the entitlement gate gains four conditions the cited source states — age 16 or over, the cared-for person receiving a qualifying disability benefit, take-home pay no more than the weekly earnings limit (a new £204 parameter), and not being in full-time education — and I verified those clauses verbatim in the pinned corpus ("you must be aged 16 or over", "The person you care for must get a qualifying disability benefit", "Your 'take home pay' cannot be more than £204 a week"). Pre-fix, a Scottish carer earning £600 a week or caring for someone on no disability benefit was paid the full annualised rate, so this is a fidelity correction and not merely coverage the module never claimed: the module already claimed to compute the CSP amount and cited SSI 2023/302 reg 5. I could not refute the fidelity classification — mechanical fails because formulas, rule set, period and entitlement logic all changed. The kind is genuinely contested, however: the same diff removes two ungrounded gate terms (`carer_support_payment_in_effect` and `or reported_carers_allowance_for_year > 0`) and re-grounds a formula whose `source:` was "PolicyEngine UK carer_support_payment final receipt wrapper", which is textbook untraceable_branch; I keep unrepresented_clause because the added source-stated conditions are the larger share of the formula change and are what the PR message names.

triage.verifier_notes:
Source verified through the pinned release (corpus_release uk-rulespec-2026-07-12, commit 3cc9219ac4): uk/guidance/mygovscot/carer-support-payment/who-can-apply = "You can apply for Carer Support Payment if you provide unpaid care for 35 hours or more a week and you must be aged 16 or over. You must usually live in Scotland. The person you care for must get a qualifying disability benefit."; .../if-you-work = "Your 'take home pay' cannot be more than £204 a week." The diff's new parameter carries the excerpt "take home pay' cannot be more than £204 a week" and formula 204.

Reviewer decision point on kind. This one module change carries two defect kinds at once:
(1) unrepresented_clause — four source-stated conditions added (age, qualifying disability benefit, £204 earnings cap, full-time education);
(2) untraceable_branch — the pre-fix formula's `carer_support_payment_in_effect` rollout switch and `or reported_carers_allowance_for_year > 0` proxy are removed, and the rule's `source:` changes from "PolicyEngine UK carer_support_payment final receipt wrapper over Carer Support Payment Regulations 2023 regs. 5 and 16" to mygov.scot guidance. The commit subject ("ground policy surfaces in ingested sources") and the maintainer comment ("those surfaces are the old pattern this PR removes (\"PolicyEngine-alignment surface… used by PolicyEngine UK and HBAI\", `reported_*` inputs)") both frame the fix as de-grounding a model-derived surface, which favors untraceable_branch. If the corpus wants one label per case and prefers the kind the commit message emphasizes, reclassify to untraceable_branch; if it prefers the kind with the most added source-traceable meaning, keep unrepresented_clause.

Note also that the 35-hour condition quoted in the first reader's PR-body quote was ALREADY present pre-fix (`weekly_care_hours >= carer_support_payment_minimum_weekly_care_hours`); only the £204 half of that quote is new, so the quote overstates the delta slightly.

Two side changes that are not defect fixes and should not drive the kind: effective_from moves from '2026-04-06' to '0001-01-01' (less precise, not a wrong_period correction), and the main derived rule's period changes from Year to Week with a new annualising wrapper. Also, the added `not person_is_in_full_time_education` term has no basis in the resolved who-can-apply slice I read (its proof atoms cite only the 35-hour and age-16 excerpts) — that is a possible post-fix grounding gap, not evidence about the pre-fix defect.
